newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares firm 0.68 pct, off highs.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares firm 0.68 pct, off highs.

text.p: Istanbul shares continued to post selective gains on Tuesday amid positive sentiment after shaking off last week's political concerns, but fell from day's highs on technical resistance, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,471, up 10 points, or 0.68 percent from Monday when it gained 1.25 percent. Profit-taking began after it brushed 1,506 in the afternoon.
Trade volume jumped to 33.27 trillion lira from Monday's 23.14 trillion.

"The market had difficulty overcoming the 1,500 barrier which prompted tehcnical selling although there were no negative news. The results of the Treasury auction were positive," said Murat Iman from Ata securities.

The Treasury sold 217.7 trillion lira of one-year bonds at 109.02 percent yield, down from a record 380.1 trillion lira sale and 112.86 percent yield in the previous 287-day bill auction on February 25.

Brokers said the market awaited Thursday's cabinet meeting where measures to combat rising Islamist activism are expected to be discussed, following a National Security Council (MGK) statement on February 28 which urged action against what the army saw as rising Islamist zeal.
Tension which had mounted early last week due to a row between the coalition's Islamist wing and the secularist army eased considerably after Erbakan signed the MGK statement last Wednesday.

Of the 237 shares traded, 94 advanced, 79 declined and 64 finished stable. The IMKB Industrial firmed 0.47 percent to 1,511, the IMKB Services gained 0.83 percent to 1,330 and the IMKB Financial edged 0.39 percent up to 1,540.
Actives were led by largely state owned firms -- flat steel giant Eregli, down 250 lira at 18,000, oil refiner Tupras, up 2,000 lira at 55,000 and Turkish Airlines, up 2,000 lira at 33,000.
They were followed by utility Aktas Elektrik, up 5,000 lira at 172,500 and leading durables producer Arcelik, up 750 lira at 17,500.
Volume in most heavily traded five stocks made up 27 percent of the total.
